author: high4
claim: Prove the converse by parity-coloring paths from one root in each connected component; use the odd-closed-walk lemma to establish parity consistency and to force every edge to cross the two parity classes.
evidence: For two root-to-vertex paths of different parity, following one and reversing the other creates an odd closed walk. For an edge whose endpoints have the same root-path parity, the two root paths plus that edge create an odd closed walk. Thus, when odd cycles are absent, path parity is well defined and every edge joins opposite classes.

subgoals: odd closed walk contains odd cycle

glossary.G: the finite undirected graph under consideration

author: high7
claim: The direct spanning-forest decomposition is solved: both implications have complete self-contained proofs and can be assembled into the target theorem.
evidence: The only-if implication is class alternation. The if implication is rooted spanning-forest depth parity plus exclusion of a monochromatic edge by its odd fundamental cycle.
